solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old country beginning to stir very early in the morning

indicators.note: the beginning of the word stir supplies just its opening letter

parts.note: one o'clock in the morning is 1 AM, with the figure 1 written as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone recalls stirring before dawn in a faraway old land.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 AM is read as I AM, the numeral one doubling as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Siam was the former name of Thailand until 1939, so it is a country of the past.

clue.text: Mess about as one coming before tailor

explanation.surface: Fiddling around like the figure who precedes the tailor in a nursery rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: The counting rhyme runs 'Tinker, tailor, soldier, sailor', so tinker comes just before tailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To tinker is to fiddle aimlessly with something; in the children's counting rhyme the mender of pots is named first, before the tailor.

clue.text: Brought up in sombre district

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across the words sombre district

explanation.surface: Someone was raised in a gloomy neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Bred is a past participle meaning reared or raised, like a child or animal.

clue.text: Like worker crossing lake at an angle

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
L is the map abbreviation for lake
a worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: An insect crosses a pond on a slant.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslant is an adverb meaning slanting or obliquely, tilted to one side.

clue.text: Secret of criminal being exempt from punishment?

indicators.note: a criminal arrangement is a crooked one, so the letters are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: A felon's secret is that he got away unpunished.
explanation.definitionFit: Going scot-free is an idiom for escaping without penalty or harm.

clue.text: Foul grown-up and her mate, no hard male

parts.note: an adult is a grown-up

indicators.note: no means without, so the named letters are dropped from the phrase her mate

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An unpleasant adult and her partner, minus the tough guy.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing H and M from HERMATE leaves ERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulterate is to foul or contaminate something by adding impure matter, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Relation dumped outside home? That's ominous

indicators.note: the relative is put around the outside of the word for home

parts.note: a sister is a relation
in means at home

explanation.surface: A family member left out of doors is a menacing sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister describes something threatening or suggesting harm, a direct synonym.

clue.text: News — it comes up accompanied by sounds

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
dings are ringing sounds, as of bells

explanation.surface: Information rising up with noises accompanying it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings is an old-fashioned word for news or information.

clue.text: Separate church finally accepted in diocese

indicators.note: the church and final letter are placed inside the bishop's territory

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word accepted

explanation.surface: A breakaway church is at last allowed within the diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is to withdraw formally from a union or body, so to separate.

clue.text: Donkey stabled by son and daughter is cured

indicators.note: stabled means housed, so the animal sits between the two family letters

parts.note: moke is a British slang word for a donkey

explanation.surface: A family of two looks after a donkey which has recovered.
explanation.definitionFit: Cured meat or fish preserved over a fire is smoked, so cured stands for it.

clue.text: Bit of a heart-throb exciting to ladies

indicators.note: exciting stirs things up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: A dreamboat thrilling to women.
explanation.definitionFit: Diastole is the phase of the heartbeat when the heart relaxes and fills, one part of each throb.

clue.text: Writer, if amiss, could get eternal censure

indicators.note: amiss means wrongly arranged, so the letters of eternal censure are jumbled

explanation.surface: An author whose wayward work might earn everlasting condemnation.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: the writer's name, rearranged, gives eternal censure.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was the eighteenth-century novelist who wrote Tristram Shandy.

clue.text: Giving a reason for financial processing

explanation.surface: Explaining oneself in the language of bookkeeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounting for something is explaining it; accounting is also the keeping of financial records.

clue.text: Anxious listener starts to get emotional inside

indicators.note: the opening letters go inside the hearing organ

parts.note: an ear is a listener, the organ that hears

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letters of get and emotional

explanation.surface: A nervous confidant begins to become tearful.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious can mean keen or impatient to do something, the sense of eager.

clue.text: Fish dish not very good — dodgy business

indicators.note: not means the pious letters are left out of the seafood dish

parts.note: scampi is a dish of breaded langoustines, served in British pubs
pi, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good

explanation.surface: A seafood meal that disappoints turns out to be a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a fraudulent scheme or racket, a slang synonym.

clue.text: Frightfully vile dame of a bygone era

indicators.note: frightfully suggests the letters are in a terrible state and must be reordered

explanation.surface: An awful old lady who belongs in history.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval refers to the Middle Ages, a period long past, so of an earlier era.

clue.text: Sweet lord often on the box

explanation.surface: A kindly peer frequently seen on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar is a sweetener; Lord Alan Sugar is the British business peer who fronts TV's The Apprentice.

clue.text: Revolutionary sort of tyre that's about to be introduced

indicators.note: introduced means brought in, so the letter for about goes into the tyre

parts.note: a radial is a type of car tyre
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A groundbreaking kind of tyre is about to be launched.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical is someone who wants sweeping political change, as a revolutionary does.

clue.text: The Cockney man spotted in the auditorium, a hairy fellow

indicators.note: in a hall of listeners, what matters is how the words are heard

parts.note: a Cockney drops the H, so he saw becomes 'e saw

explanation.surface: A Londoner noticed a shaggy man among the theatre audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech, the London dialect, drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Esau, Jacob's twin, is described as a hairy man.

clue.text: Students sauntered around having swallowed a drug naughtily

indicators.note: naughtily suggests misbehaviour, so the combined letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Students wandered about after taking illegal substances.
explanation.definitionFit: Undergraduates are university students working toward a first degree.

clue.text: What some eat for breakfast, being more reckless?

explanation.surface: Wondering if a bacon slice at breakfast makes you more daring.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasher is a slice of bacon; rasher also means more hasty or reckless.

clue.text: A doc with collection of old books, one held to be skilful

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor, a doc

indicators.note: the numeral one is held within the collection of books

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A doctor with ancient texts is considered handy.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means dexterous or clever with the hands or mind.

clue.text: Drew attention to sweet courses being passed around

indicators.note: passed around suggests turning back the other way, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: desserts are the sweet courses of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone highlighted the puddings being handed round the table.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress something is to emphasise it, so stressed means emphasised.

clue.text: Avoid failure on the cricket field

explanation.surface: Dodging a disaster at the cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck is to dodge; in cricket a duck is a batsman's score of zero, a failure.

clue.text: Sensual festive occasion with four passing out

indicators.note: passing out means leaving, so the four letters drop from the celebration

parts.note: a carnival is a festive occasion
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A steamy party where a quartet faints.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnal relates to bodily and physical desires, a synonym for sensual.

clue.text: Affected manners of couples not keeping quiet

indicators.note: not keeping means the quiet letter is dropped

parts.note: pairs are couples
P, for piano, is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: Pretentious pairs who will not stay silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on airs means behaving with pretension, showing affected manners.

clue.text: Trendy chum who may be locked up?

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
a mate is a chum

explanation.surface: A fashionable friend could end up in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is a prisoner, someone confined behind bars.

clue.text: Weep when Stan's partner gets stuck in pit

indicators.note: the comic partner is lodged inside the word for weep

parts.note: to cry is to weep
Oliver Hardy, Ollie, was the comedy partner of Stan Laurel

explanation.surface: Tears flow when the comic partner is trapped in a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A colliery is a coal mine, and a pit is the British word for one.
